name: settings-dialog
description: A Settings button opens a form dialog. Does the agent install litt's dialog, input, checkbox and button and compose them, with nothing off-system?
prompt:
The home page of this app is still the Vite starter. Replace it with a simple home for the studio (the litt.design wordmark, a heading and a line of intro) and put a Settings button top right. Clicking it opens a dialog with a small form: display name, email, and a checkbox for whether I get an email when a build finishes. Save and Cancel at the bottom. Save can just close the dialog and show a quick confirmation on the page.

This is for litt.design, our own studio site, not a client job, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the home page as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide) and the open-* screenshots (after clicking Settings, 1440 wide). Claims:
1. page: the home page is real content with a visible Settings button whose icon (if it has one) sits on the same line as its label. It is not the Vite starter (no logos, no 'Get started', no counter button).
2. page: the layout is left-aligned and airy, with generous empty space. It is not a centered stack.
3. open: a dialog panel sits above the page with a title such as Settings, a display name field, an email field, and a notifications checkbox with a visible text label.
4. open: every field has its label above it (not only a placeholder). The inputs are roomy (about 44px tall) and only slightly rounded (about 4px corners).
5. open: Save and Cancel are at the bottom right of the panel, Save last. Save is the only accent-filled button on the screen; Cancel is a neutral button with no color fill. The focus ring may also use the accent color; a checked checkbox is filled with the text color, not the accent.
6. open: the panel is a floating surface with slightly rounded corners (about 8px), a hairline edge and a soft glow or shadow with no hard offset. The page behind it is dimmed or tinted.
7. All screenshots: no text is bold: running text is regular weight, and only titles, buttons and small labels step up, to medium or semibold, there are no emoji and no decorative gradients, and in the dark screenshots the text and the panel edge are still clearly legible. The one soft light from the top (litt's light source, a faint tint that fades down a surface) is not a decorative gradient: allow it once per view.
